text:
anya: quick pulse check — saw a customer hit read-amplification in our active-active run when proxies prefetch hot keys into other regions after a write. should proxies suppress cross-region prefetch when a tenant is residency-restricted?
kevin: numbers? how bad is the amplification?
anya: roughly 3x read ops for that tenant during peak (writes triggered prefetch in two extra regions). increased bill and added regional network egress.
matt: i suspected this. our prefetch currently fires on write success and fans out to all warm regions for the model KV. it doesn't consider residency flags.
julie: tradeoff: if we suppress prefetch, cold reads in secondary regions will see higher latency. but legal/residency > latency for some customers.
sam: recommended interface: add a short header / control flag the proxy can set per-request: `X-Residency-Prefetch: allow|suppress|async-local`. proxies respect tenant-level policy unless overridden by admin. default = allow.
anya: that seems reasonable. `async-local` = still warm in-region background job, but never cross-region.
arkhip: runtime concerns: proxies currently only consult control-plane on connect; we cache tenant flags for 5m. for strict residency we probably need shorter TTL and an invalidation channel.
kevin: where do we store this flag? control-plane metadata (tenant record) or runtime routing table?
matt: control-plane tenant record + a lightweight subscription (pubsub) to proxies for delta invalidation. TTL fallback 30s if no push.
julie: legal-bot: @legal-bot any concerns if we still send non-PII cache hints cross-region? customer asked for residency for "all inference-related data".
legal-bot: if customer sets residency-strict we must avoid any cross-region copies of request/response content. cache keys derived from request body count as derived data — treat as restricted.
sam: ok — implementation plan: (1) add `residency_prefetch` boolean on tenant record; (2) proxy consults on request and sets header `X-Residency-Prefetch: suppress` when true; (3) if header==suppress, skip cross-region prefetch and only queue in-region async warm tasks; (4) add delta push channel from control-plane to proxies, fallback TTL 30s.
anya: operational notes: add metric `prefetch.cross_region_suppressed` and `prefetch.write_amplification_ratio` so SRE can alert if suppression spikes. also add a canary run with 5 tenants tomorrow.
kevin: question: what about existing tenant rollouts? need migration path — default to allow unless tenant opted-in to strict.
matt: agreed. migrator script: set `residency_prefetch=false` by default. ops will flip per-tenant.
arkhip: note: implement unit test for fallback queue and ensure KV warm tasks don't leak payloads to other regions (sanitize logs).
julie: also add an entry in the privacy runbook for residency-prefetch behavior.
anya: action items: @sam implement header+proxy behavior, @matt wire control-plane flag+pubsub, @kevin add metrics and alert, @julie update runbook, @arkhip add tests. we will check progress next sync. :thumbsup:
anya: tl;dr: suppress cross-region prefetch on residency-strict tenants, provide `async-local` warm path, expose header, short TTL + invalidation.
